mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4% over the next month reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns in the following 20-day window.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by 0.25% over the next 30 days
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the prior 30-day period of lower rates (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a labor market strengthening that boosts investor confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10,000 jobs while UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points within the next 30 days
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant correlation with the labor strength signal (Pearson IC > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden surge in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) accompanied by a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a shift from supply-side to demand-side expansion, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positively in the following 5-day horizon.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 5% while INDPRO falls by > 5% within the next 3 days
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite the demand/supply cross signal (IC < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) over three consecutive months suggests supply-side weakness that lags behind demand, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than during the prior 20-day window of expansion (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of the CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 2%, the anticipation of future rate hikes reduces equity valuations, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negatively correlated with the inflation signal (Pearson IC > 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for two consecutive months indicates a strong labor market that supports economic growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE remains below 4% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are flat or negative despite sustained labor strength (IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in both consumer confidence (HOUST) and retail sales (not available in the provided proxies – thus this sketch is invalid per the rules) cannot be constructed. Instead, a valid demand signal using available proxies: A rapid rise in housing starts proxy (not available) – so we use demand via HOUST and RSAFS: When HOUST jumps > 8% in a month while RSAFS (retail sales proxy) rises by > 5%, it suggests robust demand that drives positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 8% and RSAFS increases by > 5% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns show no significant correlation with the demand signal (IC < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising), S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days are typically negative due to discounting of future cash flows, regardless of other macro signals.
failure_condition: More than 60% of 5-day forward returns are positive during periods classified as tightening (by FEDFUNDS trend).
